answer: A call at parameter mf on a stream of volume V makes s smaller calls at parameter f, each on a stream of volume V/W (rut). Writing C(f) for the time per unit volume, the children cost (s/W)C(f) per unit of parent volume, so C(mf) is at most (s/W)C(f)+O(1) (rut). Unrolling this over the levels gives a geometric sum with ratio s/W whose deepest term is f^(log_m(s/W)) (rut). That exponent is below 1 exactly when s/W < m, i.e. s < Wm; at equality the cost is proportional to Vf and nothing is saved (rut). The number s is the total rank of the frame changes along the edges of a fixed linear exchange network (buneret, gepupog), and a frame change of rank a costs a smaller calls because a shear of rank a takes exactly a interchanges of fields (pogotos). The nested subspace labels (pukezad) give s = Wm - (N - 2L) in the bit network, with L/N = 100/539 below 1/2, so s is strictly less than Wm. The relative deficit is about 1.5e-11, so the exponent is only slightly below 1, and an explicit tau = 1 - 2^(-50) works (rut). The whole saving therefore hinges on the single strict inequality s < Wm: it makes the exponent of the recursion strictly below one.

citations.quote: Both tape primitives (the interchange of two address chunks of $u$ digits and the sifigeg on up to $d$ axes) cost the volume times a power below one of their width, because a call at parameter $mf$ makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$ on streams of volume $V/W$ with $s<Wm$
The children cost $s(V/W)\mathcal C(f)$, which per unit of the parent's volume is $(s/W)\mathcal C(f)$
The deepest term is $(s/W)^{\log_m f}=f^{\log_m(s/W)}$; for $s/W>1$ the geometric sum is a constant times it, and for $s/W\le1$ it is $O(\log f)$.
If $s=Wm$, depth $j$ contributes $m^j$, the sum is about $f$, and the cost is proportional to $Vf$: no saving.
The exponent $\log_m(s/W)=1+\log_m(1-\eta)$ is below $1$ exactly when $\eta>0$, and $\eta$ is fixed with the network.
Summing over edges, the call makes $s$ calls at parameter $f$, each on volume $V/W$, where $s$ is the total rank of the edge changes.
Hence $s_{\rm b}=W_{\rm b}m-(N-2L_{\rm b})$ and $s_{\rm c}=W_{\rm c}m-(2N-2L_{\rm c})$, both below $Wm$ because $L_{\rm b}/N=100/539$ and $L_{\rm c}/N=101/539$ are below $1/2$.
The deficit $W_{\rm b}m-s_{\rm b}=N-2L_{\rm b}=\frac{339}{539}N$ is positive as $L_{\rm b}/N<1/2$, but tiny
For $A$ in a fixed finite set, it can be performed with exactly $a$ interchanges of $b$-digit fields and $O(V)$ further work.
So any fixed $\tau<1$ with $s/W<m^\tau$ gives $\mathcal C(f)=O(f^\tau)$, and an interchange costs $O(Vf^\tau)$.

A linear exchange network is a fixed circuit of linear gates on wires, each carrying one scalar, that swaps two banks of values with a sign and restores every scratch wire to its initial value, whatever that was
